item.research_question: Can a varying stress-field ramping (VS-FR) loading sequence reduce the magnetic field levels required for complete reversible martensitic transformation in NiCoMnIn meta-magnetic shape memory alloys to below 2 T, and how does microstructure influence this requirement?
item.material_system: Ni44.8Co5.0Mn36.0In14.1 at.% single crystals (nominal Ni45Co5Mn36.6In13.4), specifically comparing Solution Heat Treated (SHT) and Secondary Annealed (SHT + 873 K 30 min) conditions.
item.processing_route: Vacuum induction melting of high purity constituents; single crystal growth via Bridgman method under He; Solution Heat Treatment (SHT) at 1173 K for 24 hours followed by water quench; Secondary annealing at 873 K for 30 min followed by water quench; samples cut to 4 mm × 4 mm × 8 mm with [001] austenite orientation.
item.test_conditions: Isothermal constant stress and stress-varying magnetic field ramping; temperatures of 263 K (SHT) and 291 K (SHT+873K); strain rate of 2.5 · 10−5 s−1; magnetic field ramp rate ≤ 50 Oe s−1; field applied collinear to stress along [001] direction.
key_findings: The SHT sample achieved complete martensite to austenite transformation under only 1.3 T applied magnetic field.
The SHT + 873 K 30 min sample required 3 T to achieve complete transformation using the VS-FR sequence.
The VS-FR sequence reduced magnetic hysteresis from 4 T (in CS-FR) to nearly zero for the secondary annealed sample.
Entropy changes of 14.7 J kg−1 K−1 (SHT) and 22 J kg−1 K−1 (SHT+873K) were generated under low fields.
Transformation strain reached 5.35% for SHT and 5.59% for SHT+873K under magnetic field ramping.
The Clausius-Clapeyron slope was 2.2 MPa K−1 for SHT and 3.16 MPa K−1 for SHT+873K.
The SHT sample exhibited a transformation hardening of 7 MPa, while the SHT+873K sample showed 27 MPa.
The transition range (Ms − Mf) was 22 K for SHT and 50 K for SHT+873K.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the lower field requirement in the SHT sample to smaller transformation hardening and a narrower transition range, caused by smaller L21 morphology (≤30 nm) without clear anti-phase boundaries (APBs). In contrast, the secondary annealed sample has large L21 domains separated by APBs which act as pinning sites for martensite propagation, increasing hardening and requiring higher fields. The VS-FR process minimizes magnetic hysteresis by applying and removing the magnetic field under different stress levels, effectively lowering the energy barrier for transformation.
item.limitations: The exact correlation between martensite crystal structure dependence on austenite ordering is not fully understood, and the specific link between transformation hardening, crystallographic order, and martensite variant size scales requires more work.
item.future_work: The authors state that the reasons for the difference in entropy change between the two microstructures will be discussed in future works, and that designing a solid-state refrigerator applying the VS-FR loading sequence will be the topic of a follow-up publication.
quotes: The complete martensite to austenite transformation was achieved with only 1.3 T in Ni45Co5Mn36.6In13.4 (at.%) single crystals.
Employing a varying stress state while field ramping (as opposed to constant stress) effectively reduces magnetic hysteresis in the Ni45Co5Mn36.6In13.4 (at.%) MMSMAs from 4 T to nearly zero.

Achieving the complete transformation under a magnetic field of only 1.3 T can be attributed to the small transformation hardening (and Ms − Mf transition temperature range) of only 7 MPa in the SHT sample.
